How to Use / Thane Creek

Exploring the Wetland Watch Platform

Thane Creek Wetland Watch is an interactive GIS-based platform designed to make wetland information easier to explore and understand. It brings together spatial information, historical comparisons, bird records and environmental threat information within a single digital interface.

Users can navigate between the website's sections to explore different aspects of the Thane Creek wetland landscape. The Monitor section provides an overview of available wetland information, while Change focuses on temporal and spatial transformations. Bird Habitats presents information about migratory and resident birds and their ecological dependence on wetlands. Threats highlights environmental pressures that may affect these ecosystems.

Users can interact with the available map layers, indicators, charts and site information to examine patterns and compare observations. The platform is intended for students, researchers, educators, conservation groups and interested members of the public. It serves as an educational and exploratory resource; interpretations should consider data sources, observation periods and the limitations of available information.

Step-by-step guide

1

Open Monitor

Start on the dashboard to explore the wetland map and statistics.

2

Choose a year

Select 2015, 2020 or 2025 to view available map information.

3

Choose a wetland

Select Panje, NRI Complex, TSC, BPS or Airoli.

4

Explore details

Use Overview, Change, Bird Records, Threats, References and Photos tabs.

5

Review other sections

Use the top navigation to learn about change, bird habitats, threats and the project.
